newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Romania approves Bulgarian nuclear fuel shipments.
newsitem.headline: Romania approves Bulgarian nuclear fuel shipments.

text.p: Bulgaria's electricity company (NEC) said on Friday Romania had given permission for transportation of Russian nuclear fuel on the River Danube for its Kozloduy nuclear plant.
The NEC said in a statement that Bucharest had licensed transportation of fresh nuclear fuel on the Danube through Romanian territory until September 2001.
Experts from the two countries have agreed on the transportation procedure and taxes that Bulgaria will pay, the statement said.

Romania was insisting on approving nuclear fuel transportation on the Danube. Last year Romanian Danube shipping authorities detained a barge carrying 106 tonnes of fresh fuel from Ukraine to Kozloduy.
Since the break-up of the Soviet Union, Bulgaria has also needed the consent of Ukraine and Moldova to transit its fuel supplies across their territory.
NEC officials said they had been in the process of negotiating consignments of Russian nuclear fuel across the territories of Ukraine and Moldova.
Bulgaria, which imports 80 percent of its energy resources, relies on its Soviet-made Kozloduy four 440-megawatt reactors and two 1,000-megawatt reactors for more than half its energy.
The officials said fresh fuel would be delivered by air for recharging the Kozloduy VVER-1,000 reactor number six at the end of September or the beginning of October.
This will be the second delivery by air. Fuel for recharging the Kozloduy VVER-440 reactors from Russia was sent by air for the first time three months ago.
